text:
derek.v: Customer 'acme-ml' opened a Sev2 — their app containers started getting NXDOMAIN for svc.internal.redwood when resolving the private service after we migrated their VPC to a new account. From their app: DNS fails; from a bastion in the same VPC it resolves to a public IP. Very likely split-horizon/hosted-zone overlap but need quick triage.

sarah.k: Can we get the VPC ID + account? Also ask them to run these quick checks in the app pod and a bastion: 
`dig svc.internal.redwood +short` 
`dig svc.internal.redwood @10.0.0.2 +short` (VPC resolver) 
`nslookup svc.internal.redwood`

ben.t: Also curl with sni to see TLS: 
`curl -v --resolve svc.internal.redwood:443:3.4.5.6 https://svc.internal.redwood/` 
or openssl: `openssl s_client -connect 3.4.5.6:443 -servername svc.internal.redwood`

derek.v: Got outputs from customer. App pod (inside k8s) `dig` shows NXDOMAIN. Bastion (same VPC) shows IP 3.4.5.6. They pasted results: 
```
# app pod
$ dig svc.internal.redwood +short

; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc.internal.redwood +short
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 12345

# bastion (same subnet)
$ dig svc.internal.redwood +short
3.4.5.6
```

ben.t: Thanks. That pattern usually means the node's resolver or search path is different (e.g., node-local cache, coredns stub, or a conditional forwarder). Which k8s DNS do they run? kube-dns / coredns?

derek.v: They run node-local DNS + coredns. Pod's /etc/resolv.conf points to 169.254.25.10 (node-local). Host resolves correctly.

elise.s: Node-local can be configured to forward to a different resolver; I've seen it return NXDOMAIN if it points to a VPC resolver that has a resolver rule forwarding that suffix to a wrong account. Steps to triage: 
- From the node-local IP (pod), run `dig @169.254.25.10 svc.internal.redwood +trace` and `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.internal.redwood`
- Check Route53: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`"svc.internal.redwood."`]'` and `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZXXXX` then `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZXXX --query VPCs` to see associated VPCs and accounts.

sarah.k: Another angle: customer said we recently migrated the VPC into a different AWS account and set up cross-account VPC sharing. If there's a private hosted zone with the same name in the _old_ account and it's still associated with the VPC, route53 could return records from the wrong hosted zone depending on association order. Confirm there are no overlapping private zones across accounts.

derek.v: Customer ran `dig @169.254.25.10 svc.internal.redwood +short` and got NXDOMAIN. `dig @10.0.0.2 svc.internal.redwood +short` returns 3.4.5.6. So node-local -> NXDOMAIN, VPC resolver -> correct IP.

ben.t: That nails it: node-local DNS is likely forwarding to a resolver that returns NXDOMAIN (maybe a conditional forwarder to an on-prem DNS or a resolver rule). Ask for node-local config: `kubectl -n kube-system get configmap node-local-dns -o yaml` and coredns configmap. Also: `cat /etc/resolv.conf` inside the pod and on the node.

derek.v: Customer pasted node-local config: forward plugin points to 192.0.2.53 (forwarder) for suffix `internal.redwood`. 192.0.2.53 is an IP of their old resolver in previous account which is no longer reachable for this suffix — returns NXDOMAIN.

elise.s: Ok that explains NXDOMAIN. Action items: 
- Have customer remove conditional forward for `internal.redwood` from node-local/coredns so queries hit the VPC resolver (10.0.0.2) or update forwarder to point to the correct resolver that can answer the private hosted zone. 
- Alternatively, associate the correct Route53 private hosted zone with the VPC if missing.

sarah.k: Also check TLS implications: since bastion resolves to 3.4.5.6 (correct internal IP) but pods didn't, if they somehow hit the public IP path, TLS cert from public endpoint may not match internal SAN. Ben, did the openssl output show cert mismatch?

ben.t: They ran `openssl s_client -connect 3.4.5.6:443 -servername svc.internal.redwood` and got cert for `svc.redwood.com` (public). curl from pod gave: `SSL: certificate subjectAltName does not match`. So some clients are hitting the public (or external) listener which serves a different cert. That makes sense if some paths resolve to public IP.

derek.v: Customer will remove the stale forwarder and confirm. They've already associated the private hosted zone in the new account but the node-local forwarder still points at old resolver.

elise.s: Good. Recommend these final remediation steps to customer: 
1) Update node-local/coredns forwarders to use VPC resolver (or delete conditional forwarder for `.internal.redwood`).
2) Confirm Route53 private hosted zone is associated with the correct VPC(s) and no overlapping private zones exist in other accounts: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones --query 'HostedZones[?Name==`"internal.redwood."`]'` and inspect `VPCs` for each zone.
3) If TLS errors remain, run `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername svc.internal.redwood` from pod/node to confirm cert.
4) If they need, enable Query Logging on the private hosted zone (Route53 Resolver logs) to capture which resolver answered NXDOMAIN.

derek.v: I'll send these steps and mark P1 pending customer's confirmation. inc-bot: incident created #INC-2026 and assigned to support oncall. :spiral_calendar_pad:
